The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Public
Safety Commission with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 3rd Monday of every month at 6:00 p.m.

In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires
modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City at
(626) 300­0735 or at Fire@CityofSanMarino.org at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City will
do it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

How to view or listen to the meeting from home:
  Visit www.CityofSanMarino.org/Zoom

How to offer public comment from home:
  Public comment will be accepted by email to Fire@CityofSanMarino.org until 3:00 p.m.
  the day of the meeting. Written public comment received by 3:00 p.m. will be
  distributed to the Public Safety Commission during the meeting. Any comments
  received after 3:00 p.m. will be included in the public comment record but not provided
  to City Council at the meeting.
  Written public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us teleconference
  module during the meeting. Written Zoom comments will be accepted after the in­

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the Stoneman
Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.CityofSanMarino.org.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the Public Safety
Commission by completing a public comment card prior to the meeting. At this time, the
public may address the Public Safety Commission on items that are not on the agenda.
Pursuant to state law, the Public Safety Commission may not discuss or take action on
issues not on the meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.3). The Chair reserves
the right to place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such
items.

COMMISSIONER REPORTS

This is an opportunity for members of the Public Safety Commission to inform the public of
any meetings or conferences they may have attended.

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Public Safety Commission receive and file
  the Traffic Review for Rose Avenue from San Gabriel Blvd to Del Mar Avenue, and

  the Commission concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would
  be:

  ”I move to receive and file the attached Traffic Review prepared by Transtech for
  Rose Avenue from San Gabriel Blvd to Del Mar Avenue, and recommend staff begin
  implementation of the proposed improvments”.

2.  TRAFFIC CONDITIONS REVIEW AND REPORT ­ DUARTE ROAD FROM
  SAN GABRIEL TO LORAIN
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Public Safety Commission receive and file
  the attached Traffic Conditions Review and Report from Transtech for Duarte Road
  from San Gabriel to Lorain, and recommend beginning the implementation of the
  proposed changes. If the Commission concurs with staff’s recommendation, an
  appropriate motion would be:

  ”I move to receive and file the attached Traffic Conditions Review and Report from
  Transtech for Duarte Road from San Gabriel to Lorain, and recommend staff begin
  implementation of the proposed changes”.

3.  FIRE DEPARTMENT ANNUAL INSPECTION
  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Commission receive and file the Fire
  Department Annual Inspection report. If the Commission concurs with staff’s
  recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the Fire Department Annual Inspection report.”
